### body and surface

MDN: [`color`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/color), [`background-color`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/background-color) and [`border-color`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/border-color).

The roles, which the theme classes change.
token_color_classes:
## Classes

The patterns are `kicl-color-{name}`, `kicl-background-color-{name}` and `kicl-fill-{name}`, where `{name}` is any color above.
token_color_hues:
## Hues

The same ten steps for each hue.
token_color_intro: Use the roles under Body and surface for anything that should follow the light and dark themes. The palette is for a color that stays the same in both.
token_color_levels:
## Levels

The colors behind `level`, explained on [Level]({{docs}}tokens/semantics/level). Each level has four looks taken from its hue: `secondary` is step `600`, `tertiary` `700` and `ghost` `500`, and `ink`, for words on a tinted fill, is `800` on a light page and `200` on a dark one.

Warning has no hue of its own. On a light page its looks are steps of its own color, a mix of yellow and orange. On a dark page warning is plain yellow, and its looks are yellow's steps.
token_color_neutrals:
## Neutrals

Black, gray and white, each in ten steps from `50`, the lightest, to `900`, the darkest. `500` is the color itself, and `--kicl-color-grey` is the same as `--kicl-color-grey-500`. Body text and backgrounds come from these.
token_color_part_14:
`kicl-color-{name}` sets `--kicl-body-color` as well as `color`, so an icon or a border inside picks up the color too. `kicl-fill-{name}` is for SVG.

The body colors have their own:

- `kicl-color-body-color` and `kicl-fill-body-color` use the text color.
- `kicl-background-color-body` uses the page color, and `kicl-background-color-body-color` fills with the text color.
token_color_part_3: `black-pure` and `white-pure` are `#000` and `#fff`, outside the scale.
token_color_see_through:
### see-through

`black-a{n}` and `white-a{n}` are black and white at `{n}`%, from 4 to 80. `neutral-a{n}` is black on a light page and white on a dark one, at `{n}`%, for washes, hovers and quieter text. `page-a{n}` is the page's own color, for panes, scrims and fades that settle into the page. `--kicl-surface-glass-color` is a surface you can see through, for a pane with a blur behind it.
token_contrast_disabled:
## Disabled

A disabled control fades to 40% and shows a `not-allowed` cursor, and its label gets the same cursor. A disabled button also loses a little saturation. WCAG doesn't ask disabled controls to meet contrast.

A disabled fieldset doesn't fade itself, only its controls, so its legend stays readable.
token_contrast_highlights_and_placeholde:
## Highlights and placeholders

`mark` is filled with the warning color, and its text picks the color that contrasts with it (`contrast-color()`). A placeholder is the body color at 50%, which is lighter than 4.5:1 on purpose: it's a hint, so every field still needs a visible label.
token_contrast_intro: These rules keep text readable at every size. Two things go below them on purpose, disabled controls and placeholders, and both are explained below.
token_contrast_secondary_text:
## Secondary text

Secondary text, like `Text variant='secondary'`, a faded heading or a hint, is `--kicl-color-neutral-a64`, or the secondary look of its level. On the page that gives about 5.3:1 on light and 7.4:1 on dark, above the 4.5:1 WCAG AA asks of small text. A wash, like a hover, is `--kicl-color-neutral-a16`, since it sits behind text rather than being read.
token_contrast_text_size:
## Text size

Body text is 16px, and the smallest size, `smallest`, is 12px. `smaller` is 13px and `small` 14px. Sizes are in rem, so these are at the browser's default 16px and grow with the reader's settings. Body line height is 1.5.

On iOS, fields never drop below 16px, since Safari zooms the page into any smaller field when it takes focus.
token_display_classes:
## Classes

The pattern is `kicl-display-{keyword}`, where `{keyword}` is any value above.
token_display_intro: Classes that set `display` on an element that isn't laid out with the Layout component. For grid and flex layouts, use Layout and its props.
token_display_part_5:
Single keywords only: the two-value syntax, like `block flow`, has no class.

`kicl-layout` is the class the Layout component puts on its child. Use the component.
token_display_subgrid:
## Subgrid

`kicl-grid-template-rows-subgrid` makes a grid item a grid on its parent's rows, and `kicl-grid-row-span-{1…6}` says how many rows it takes. Cards in a grid line up their parts this way: each card takes as many rows as it has parts, and the tallest picture, title or description in a row sets that row for every card.

An item stretches to its row unless told otherwise: `kicl-align-self-{start|center|end|stretch}` sets where it sits in the row, and `kicl-justify-self-{start|center|end|stretch}` where it sits across its column.
token_effects_backdrop_filter:
### backdrop-filter

MDN: [`backdrop-filter`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/backdrop-filter).

The frosted pane behind the global header and anything else over a scrolling page.
token_effects_intro: Shadows, frosted panes and scrims for things that sit over the page.
token_effects_part_6:
`{name}` is `center`, `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `overlay` or `none`. `overlay` is the soft shadow under popovers and menus.

- `kicl-backdrop` is the frosted pane: what's behind is blurred and tinted with `--kicl-color-page-a12`, so text on it stays readable. A pane over one element, like a spinner's, sets `--kicl-backdrop-tint` to a stronger one, such as `--kicl-color-page-a64`.
- `kicl-backdrop-blur` blurs what's behind less than `kicl-backdrop` does, and adds no tint.
- `kicl-scrim` mutes a picture under a wash of the page color, from `--kicl-scrim-top` at the top to `--kicl-scrim-foot` at the foot. Put it on a positioned element.
token_effects_scrim:
### scrim

The scrim over a picture, so text on it stays readable.
token_focus_focus_ring:
## Focus ring

Links, buttons, fields, `summary` and `video` draw an outline from three variables. The style is `none` until the element takes keyboard focus, when `:focus-visible` switches it to `dashed`. Clicking a link or button doesn't show the ring, but clicking into a text field does, because the browser expects typing there. Tab always shows it. The color follows the theme, so the ring keeps its contrast on both.

An element that only script focuses, with `tabindex='-1'`, has no ring. That's how `#main` takes focus after a route change, so a screen reader starts at the new page without a stray outline.
token_focus_intro: Someone using the keyboard needs to see where focus is, and the fixed header shouldn't hide what they've moved to.
token_focus_out_from_under_the_header:
## Out from under the header

The global header is fixed, so the page keeps focus and anchors clear of it:

- `html` sets `scroll-padding-block-start` to the header's height, so a focused field or a jumped-to heading stops below the header, not behind it.
- `:target` adds `scroll-margin-block` of `--kicl-gutter-wide`, so a jump to an anchor never lands flush against that edge.

Neither needs a class. Same-page links scroll smoothly, unless the person asks for less motion.
token_interaction_classes:
## Classes

The patterns are `kicl-pointer-events-{keyword}`, `kicl-cursor-{keyword}`, `kicl-touch-action-{keyword}` and `kicl-user-select-{keyword}`, where `{keyword}` is the CSS value listed above.
token_interaction_intro: How an element answers the pointer and touch: its cursor, which gestures the page keeps, whether its text selects, and whether it takes clicks at all.
token_layers_how_a_stylesheet_gets_its_l:
## How a stylesheet gets its layer

Component and view stylesheets don't write `@layer` themselves. At build time, `getStyleLayer` in `Design/scripts/get-style-layer.ts` picks the layer from the file's path, and the Vite config wraps the compiled CSS in it. Each file also gets the full `@layer reset, base, layout, components, wrappers, views, utilities;` statement at the top, so whichever stylesheet loads first fixes the order, and no file has to be guaranteed to load first.

- `core/styles/styles.body.scss`, `styles.generic.scss` and `styles.headings.scss` go to `base`.
- `core/styles/layout.scss` goes to `layout`.
- Every other file in `core/styles` goes to `utilities`.
- `status/` goes to `views`.
- `components/animation/` and `components/frame/` go to `wrappers`.
- Everything else goes to `components`.
- Sass partials, whose names start with `_`, are left unwrapped, because a layer would scope their mixins and functions to that block.

The host does the same in `App/.client/helper/get-style-layer.ts`, and puts every stylesheet it compiles in `views`.
token_layers_how_layers_work:
## How layers work

A cascade layer is a named group of rules, made with the CSS `@layer` at-rule. When two declarations compete, the browser compares their layers before it looks at specificity or source order. A rule in a later layer wins over a rule in an earlier one, even when the earlier rule has the more specific selector.
token_layers_intro: Cascade layers decide which rule wins when two rules set the same property on the same element. Every stylesheet in the design system and in the host goes into one of seven layers, so the layer decides first, and load order and selector length only settle a tie inside a layer.
token_layers_part_4:
Three more rules from the spec matter here:

- **Order is set by the first `@layer` statement the browser sees.** Naming a layer again later doesn't move it.
- **Styles outside any layer beat every layer.** A stray unlayered stylesheet would win over the whole design system, which is why even the vendor resets are put in a layer.
- **`!important` reverses the order.** An important declaration in an earlier layer beats an important one in a later layer. So `!important` is for a rule that has to beat everything after it, and isn't a way to win a fight between two utilities.

The definitions are in [CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5, Cascade Layers](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-cascade-5/#layering), and MDN has a readable reference at [@layer](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/At-rules/@layer).
token_layers_the_seven_layers:
## The seven layers

Lowest first. Each layer beats every layer above it in this list.

1. **`reset`** holds the vendor resets, `normalize.css` and `reset-css`. `core/styles/reset.css` imports them with `@import ... layer(reset)`, since leaving them unlayered would put them above everything.
2. **`base`** holds element defaults: `body`, headings, form controls, focus rings and the theme classes (`styles.body.scss`, `styles.generic.scss`, `styles.headings.scss`).
3. **`layout`** holds `.kicl-layout`. It sits below `components` because `Layout` clones its classes onto the child it wraps, and the child component's own styles should win.
4. **`components`** holds every component's stylesheet, and the docs pages' own styles.
5. **`wrappers`** holds the components that put their class on a child, `Animation` and `Frame`. They sit above `components` so the wrapper's styles win over the child's.
6. **`views`** holds a host's page styles. Every stylesheet in Ki.CL goes here, and so do the design system's status pages. A view can restyle any component without raising specificity.
7. **`utilities`** holds every `kicl-*` class and the `:root` tokens in `core/styles`. A class you put on an element wins over component and view styles, so `className='kicl-padding-wide'` on a Card works without `!important`.
token_layers_when_you_write_css:
## When you write CSS

- **In a view,** write plain selectors. They're already above every component.
- **In a component,** don't raise specificity to beat another component. If one has to win, it belongs in a different layer.
- **On an element,** use a utility class. It wins over both.
- **Only use `!important`** for a rule that has to beat every later layer. Two rules use it today: the 16px floor on iOS fields in `base`, which has to stay above any `kicl-font-size-*` class, and `Animation` hiding an element that has left, which has to beat a display class on the same element.
token_layers_why_the_list_is_written_twi:
## Why the list is written twice

The host and the design system ship separate stylesheets onto one page, and the first `@layer` statement the browser reads sets the order for both. If the two lists ever differed, which one won would depend on which file loaded first. So `LAYERS` in the design system's `Design/scripts/get-style-layer.ts` and in Ki.CL's `App/.client/helper/get-style-layer.ts` must stay identical, and changing one means changing the other in the same release.
token_layers_why_we_use_them:
## Why we use them

Without layers, CSS settles a tie between two rules by specificity, then by which stylesheet came last. Both are fragile here, for three reasons.

**Load order isn't stable.** The site is two builds on one page: the host and the design system remote, loaded through Module Federation. In development, Vite injects one `<style>` per module in import order, and `core/styles` lost ties with a component's own styles. A production build splits CSS by chunk and links each chunk's dependencies first, and there the same `core/styles` won them. The same source gave opposite results. The bug that showed it: in the built site only, `.kicl-layout` beat the logo's own styles, set it to `min-block-size: 100dvb`, and pushed it out of its header.

**Specificity keeps rising.** To win a tie, a rule needs a longer selector. The utilities used to repeat their own class name (`.kicl-x.kicl-x`) for exactly that, and each fix like it raises the bar for the next rule that has to win.

**Some rules always have to win.** A class on an element, like `kicl-padding-wide`, should beat the component it's on. A view should be able to restyle a component. A vendor reset should never override the design system. None of that could be promised by specificity alone without `!important` everywhere.

Layers solve all three by deciding the winner by layer first. Load order and selector length only matter inside a layer, so a component can't beat a utility with a longer selector or a later load, and the order is the same in development, in production and in any host.
token_level_classes:
## Classes

In a component, use the `level` prop, so the label, the fill and the edge stay in step. Outside one, the same colors apply with `kicl-color-{level}`, `kicl-background-color-{level}` and `kicl-fill-{level}`, where `{level}` is `neutral`, `confirm`, `error`, `info` or `warning`, with `-secondary`, `-tertiary`, `-ghost` or `-ink` for a look.
token_level_intro:
`level` says what something means, and each level has a color: `neutral`, `confirm`, `error`, `info` and `warning`.

`neutral` is black on a light page and white on a dark one, and a component with no level takes it. The same level is the same color on Button, Badge, Card, Bubble, Heading, Text, Status, Markdown and Diagram. Status has no `neutral` or `confirm`.

Level and variant are separate props, and each component combines them its own way. A secondary error button has a faint wash of `--kicl-color-error-secondary` behind a label in that color. A card with a level colors its edge, or, when it's `tertiary`, tints its surface. The steps each level's looks come from are on [Color]({{docs}}tokens/foundations/color).

Color alone doesn't say what something means to everyone, so pair a level with words or an icon, as Status does.
token_level_variables:
## Variables

`warning` mixes yellow and orange on a light page and is plain yellow on a dark one, and `neutral` is black or white. The others point at a hue.
token_motion_body_transition:
### body transition

MDN: [`transition-duration`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/transition-duration), [`transition-property`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/transition-property) and [`transition-timing-function`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/transition-timing-function).

The body's own transition, when the theme changes.
token_motion_intro: `--kicl-transition-duration` is 600ms, and the named steps are scaled from it, from a fifth of it to eight times as long. [Reduced motion]({{docs}}tokens/accessibility/reduced-motion) covers what stops when someone asks for less motion. Easing curves are named by family and direction.
token_motion_part_8:
`{step}` is `fastest`, `faster`, `fast`, `slow`, `slower`, `slowest` or `extreme`. Leave it out for the default. The longer durations, `6s` to `5m`, are variables only.

Easing has no classes. Read it in CSS, as in `transition-timing-function: var(--kicl-ease-quad-out)`.

- `kicl-scroll-reveal` fades and slides an element in from below as it scrolls into view. `kicl-scroll-reveal-start` and `kicl-scroll-reveal-end` bring it in from the inline start or end.
- `kicl-animation-none` stops an element's own animation, such as a skeleton standing in for something that isn't loading.
- `kicl-animation-none-reduced-motion` stops an element's animation when the person asks for less motion.
- `kicl-visibility-hidden-reduced-motion` hides something that only makes sense with motion.
token_motion_scroll_reveal:
### scroll-reveal

MDN: [`animation-timeline`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/animation-timeline).

The scroll reveal, and the slowly panning five-color gradient used on the scroll indicator.
token_overflow_intro: How an element treats content that runs past its box, how scrolling carries on past it, and how far its layout is kept separate from the rest of the page.
token_overflow_part_8:
`{keyword}` for overflow is `auto`, `clip`, `hidden`, `scroll` or `visible`. For contain it's `none`, `content`, `inline-size`, `layout`, `paint`, `size` or `strict`.

`kicl-contain-inline-size` stops an element's content from widening its parent. A parent sized to fit its content then takes its width from its other children, and this element fits inside that width.

- `kicl-scrollbar-none` hides the scrollbar and keeps the scrolling.
- `kicl-scroll-fade` fades the content out at the top and bottom edges it can scroll toward, and hides the scrollbar. `kicl-scroll-fade-inline` does the same at the start and end, for a row that scrolls sideways.
- `kicl-stuck-line-start` and `kicl-stuck-line-end` draw the slowly panning five-color gradient used on the scroll indicator along a sticky element's edge while it's stuck: `start` for a footer stuck to the bottom, `end` for a header stuck to the top.
token_position_classes:
## Classes

The pattern is `kicl-position-{keyword}`, where `{keyword}` is any value above.
token_position_intro: Classes that set `position`. Place the element with the inset classes on [Sides]({{docs}}tokens/semantics/sides).
token_reduced_motion_intro: When someone sets their system to reduce motion, the components below stop animating on their own and still show their end state. Two classes cover anything else that moves.
token_reduced_motion_part_4:
- `kicl-animation-none-reduced-motion` stops an element's own animation.
- `kicl-visibility-hidden-reduced-motion` hides something that only works with motion. Pair it with `kicl-animation-none-reduced-motion` when an animation sets `visibility`.

Write anything new that moves inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so it's off unless the person is happy with motion.
token_reduced_motion_what_changes_by_its:
## What changes by itself

- `Animation` cuts its duration to nothing, so the end state and its events still arrive.
- Frames, sheets, the segmented control's thumb and skeleton shimmer stop animating.
- `kicl-scroll-reveal` content just shows, without sliding in.
- Same-page links jump instead of scrolling smoothly, and the global header stops sliding.
token_sides_classes:
## Classes

A class that sets one side names the axis, then the edge, then the step: `kicl-{property}-{axis}-{edge}-{step}`.

- `{axis}` is `block` or `inline`. Leave it out for both axes.
- `{edge}` is `start` or `end`. Leave it out for both edges of the axis.
- `{step}` is a gutter step, listed on [Spacing]({{docs}}tokens/semantics/spacing). Leave it out for the default.

So `kicl-padding` is all four sides, `kicl-padding-block` is top and bottom, and `kicl-padding-block-start` is the top alone. Padding, margin and inset all follow this order.
token_sides_inset:
## Inset

Inset places a positioned element, so it only has an effect on an element with a `kicl-position-*` class or another position. It takes the gutter steps and also `0` and `auto`, as `kicl-inset-{axis}-{edge}-{step}`.
token_sides_intro:
Spacing and position are written with logical properties, block and inline, start and end, rather than top or left. On a left-to-right page, `block-start` is the top, `block-end` the bottom, `inline-start` the left and `inline-end` the right. A right-to-left page flips without any change.

Popover placements and Sheet sides take the same four names, `block-start`, `block-end`, `inline-start` and `inline-end`.
token_sides_mirroring_usage: `kicl-rtl-mirror` flips an icon on a right-to-left page. Use it on icons that point along the reading direction, such as arrows. Leave out anything that means the same either way, like play buttons and clocks.
token_sides_part_4:
Some insets are named for what they line up with:

- `kicl-inset-block-start-header` sits under the global header while it shows, and at the top while it hides.

- `kicl-inset-inline-screen` stretches a positioned element to the full screen width from inside a narrower parent.

Widths come from a 12-column scale. Twelve columns are the page, at most 80rem, and a span of `n` is `n` columns plus the gaps between them, so a width lines up with a real 12-column grid. Sizes are in rem, so at the browser's default 16px root, body text is 16px and `smallest` is 12px. `large` and `larger` set the line height to 1.2, and `largest`, `huge` and `extreme` to 1, so large text sits in tighter lines than body text. `huge` and `extreme` aren't shown here, because they grow with the viewport.

## Classes

Variant is a prop, not a utility, so it has no variables or `kicl-*` classes of its own. Each component turns it into its own modifier class, `kicl--components--{component}--variant--{variant}`. Don't write those by hand. Set the prop, and the component picks the colors from its `level`, or `neutral` without one.
token_variant_intro:
`variant` says how much a component stands out, from a filled `primary` down to an outlined `ghost`.

`primary` fills with the level's color, and its label is black or white, whichever reads against that fill. `secondary` and `tertiary` put a faint, see-through wash of the level's color behind a label in that color, with `tertiary` the fainter of the two. `ghost` has no fill, only an edge and a label in the level's color.

Button, Badge, Card, Bubble, Text and Popover take it, and `InputGroupButton` takes `primary` or `ghost`. Badge has no `tertiary` and Card has no `ghost`. Card tints its own surface instead of a wash: see-through for `secondary`, solid for `tertiary`.

- `kicl-hidden` hides an element visually and leaves it for screen readers.

- `kicl-hidden-up-to-{name}` hides it visually at that breakpoint and narrower, see Breakpoints.
- `kicl-visibility-{visible|hidden|collapse}` sets `visibility`. A hidden element keeps its space and isn't read out, so items in a list stay lined up with or without it.
- `kicl-visibility-hidden-reduced-motion` hides it when the person asks for less motion.
- `kicl-print-hidden` leaves it off paper, and `kicl-print-only` shows it only on paper.

tokens_home_intro:
Tokens are the values every component is built from: color, spacing, size, type, motion and stacking. They come in two tiers.

Primitives are raw values, like `--kicl-color-blue` or `--kicl-gutter`. Roles say what a value is for, like `--kicl-body-color` or `--kicl-surface-color`, and point at a primitive.

Components should read roles rather than primitives, so a theme can restyle every component by redefining the roles, without touching the components.

The props that set how a component looks share one set of names, defined once in `design/components/spec`. Components that take one of these props draw their values from that one list. If a component can't support a value, its type leaves it out, so TypeScript rejects it instead of the component ignoring it.
tokens_home_naming:
## Naming

Most utility classes, and the variables they read, are named after the CSS property they set, then the variation: `--kicl-{property}-{variation}` for the value and `kicl-{property}-{variation}` for the class that applies it. Roles and scales are named for what they're for instead, like `--kicl-body-color` or `--kicl-gutter`.
tokens_home_part_3:
`--kicl-font-size-large` is the value, and `kicl-font-size-large` sets `font-size` to it. With no variation, the class sets the default: `kicl-font-size` is `--kicl-font-size`, and `kicl-padding` is `--kicl-gutter`.

The property is the full CSS name, logical where CSS has a logical form: `inline-size` rather than width, `padding-block-start` rather than padding-top. So a side always reads in the same order, `kicl-{property}-{axis}-{edge}-{step}`:
tokens_home_part_4:
`{axis}` is `block` or `inline`, `{edge}` is `start` or `end`, and either can be left out to cover both. [Sides]({{docs}}tokens/semantics/sides) has the full list.

Spacing values come from the gutter scale, so the same step names show up everywhere a distance does: `none`, `narrowest`, `narrower`, `narrow`, the default, `wide`, `wider`, `widest` and `extreme`. Sizes use `xs` to `max`, widths use columns `1` to `12`, and keyword properties like `display` or `overflow` use the CSS keyword itself, as in `kicl-display-flex`.

Names with a double dash belong to a component, like the class `kicl--components--button--variant--primary` or the variable `--kicl-layout--gap`. Set them through its props, not by hand.

Utilities sit in the last cascade layer, so a class wins over a component's own styles without `!important`. The exceptions are the two rules that use `!important` on purpose, listed on [Cascade layers]({{docs}}tokens/foundations/layers).
